title: Navigator: find the right tool for your input
description: Find spaCR tools from a task, file or project, inspect input evidence and settings, and follow workflows into the native modules.
objectives: Find tools with local paths, file or folder drops, and case-insensitive tasks submitted with Enter.
Review input evidence, suggested settings and workflow steps before opening a native tool.
Navigate organism workflows, panels, active jobs and optional AI controls.
Distinguish measurement tables from annotation or history databases and start fresh with Home.
prerequisite: Install spaCR and open Navigator. Use the supplied example image, image folder, measured project, annotation/history-only database and saved settings file, or equivalent local inputs.

scenes.narration: Navigator starts with a search field over the spaCR theme. Open it with spacr-nav or spacr-navigator, then begin with a task, file or folder.
You can also enable Navigator from Help. Navigator is on by default; a saved choice is kept.
Use the collapsible dock to open a module directly. News and Widgets open beside the workspace while the search and description stay in place.
Type measure cells and press Enter. Matching ignores letter case. Typing alone leaves the current suggestions in place and does not start a tool.
Drop a single local image file into Navigator. It inspects the input and offers supported next steps, rather than starting a processing run.
Drop one folder to inspect its contents. Suggestions depend on the files and data already present in that folder.
For an exact location, paste a file or project path and press Enter. Browse also lets you choose a file or folder.
A measured project has data that analysis tools can read. Here, the measurement tables make tools such as Graph Builder available.
This example contains annotation and history tables, not measured features. The database filename alone does not prove measurements have been calculated.
Settings files can provide a proposed module and settings preview. Review the proposal before opening the module; Navigator does not run the analysis for you.
Choose a module card to explore its workflow. Read the description below the cards to check its purpose and required input.
Explore a next step to extend the network. Earlier branches stay visible, helping you follow the route from input through analysis and results.
Search for Toxoplasma to see its organism workflow and assay choices. Select the step that matches the data and biological question you have.
Use Back or Escape to return from a workflow to the suggestions. These navigation actions do not run an analysis or change your input files.
Open the suggested native tool when ready. Navigator passes the selected input to its matching source setting; review the settings before you press Run.
Enter running jobs and choose Running to inspect active spaCR jobs in Widgets. Open, pause and stop controls apply to the listed jobs.
The AI control is optional. Its first-use dialog lets you choose a provider. Local paths and matching tool suggestions keep their normal routes.
Home returns Navigator to a fresh search, clearing its previous suggestions and workflow. Start again with the next task or input you want to explore.
